$comment: WHO USES @broberg/sso — the list I notify on every release.
Christian's standing order, 2026-09-20: every release of this package is
announced to broberg-id AND every known consumer, at PUBLISH time — not
when somebody is about to upgrade. The day it was given, 0.2.1 had spent
an hour on npm rejecting every token the real Broberg ID issues.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS RATHER THAN A LOOKUP. Discovery is the right place to
ask 'who uses X', and it was MEASURED EMPTY for this package the same day:
131 enrolment rows, 0 mentioning sso. A rule whose data source is empty is
not a rule, it is a reminder — so the list lives here, in the repo that
publishes the package, and the release gate reads it out loud.
EVERY ENTRY CARRIES ITS EVIDENCE. `version` is what was MEASURED in their
tree, `as_of` is when, and `source` is how. An entry whose as_of is old is
visibly old rather than quietly wrong — that is the whole difference
between a register and a note.
Adding one: measure first, then write the row. Never write what a session
says it is planning to run.
A version here is what was MEASURED in their tree, never what they said they would run.

consumers.uses: examples/minimal-app only — BID ITSELF DOES NOT DEPEND ON sso (their measurement, 2026-09-20). They are the issuer, and they publish the public integration guide at id.broberg.ai/docs.md, which is what makes a wrong version number there expensive
consumers.source: their own measurement after rolling back from 0.2.1; enrolled in Discovery the same hour
consumers.notify: always, first — a release that changes verification changes their own service's story

consumers.uses: core only (createSsoClient), NOT the Hono adapter — their session is keyed on their own userId, so the adapter's own cookie would be a second opinion about who is logged in
consumers.source: their own measurement, quoted: apps/core/package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml version: 0.1.0(hono@4.13.7)
consumers.notify: always — BID's app #1, and the package is the only door into their product

notify_beyond_this_file: MEASURED BY broberg-id 2026-09-20, the whole client table at BID:
One real consumer, and it IS a cc session — so today my list and theirs
are the same set, and 'tell broberg-id, they tell the rest' costs nothing.
THAT ASSUMPTION DIES AT CUSTOMER TWO, and they said so rather than letting
it be discovered: FDAA gets its OWN tenant on its own domain, i.e. a
separate BID deployment with a client table neither they nor I can read
from here. There is no mechanism today for reaching a client that is not a
cc session, and none that spans tenants. Theirs to build; ours to stop
assuming. When a consumer appears that is not a session, this file cannot
answer the question it exists for.
